package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions distributed via Google Play Store and 9Apps during campaign)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because it covertly modifies legitimate, pre-installed applications on infected Android devices by injecting unauthorized advertisement code. This results in fraudulent ad displays, unauthorized revenue generation for the attacker, and undermines device integrity and user trust by subverting app functionality without user consent.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into pre-installed application APKs on the device (e.g., /data/app/[target_app_package]/base.apk)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime after installation, the code scans installed applications, identifies target apps, injects malicious advertisement code into their APKs, and replaces the original apps with the modified versions, resulting in unauthorized ad code execution and fraudulent ad display.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs unauthorized modification and replacement of other installed applications, which is a clear violation of Android's security model and is highly indicative of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Android apps are sandboxed and cannot alter or replace other installed applications; only system-level or device management tools with explicit user consent and elevated privileges may perform such actions, and never for ad injection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System update tools or device management software (with explicit user consent and system-level privileges) may update or patch apps, but do not inject adware or modify unrelated apps for monetization.
key_indicators: Code injection into unrelated, legitimate apps
Replacement of official app APKs with tampered versions
Unauthorized ad code insertion into system or user apps
Use of filesystem and package management permissions to alter apps

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after app launch, in background within modified app)
execution_context.file_location: Injected code within modified apps (e.g., inside classes.dex of tampered APKs)
required_permissions: display overlays (to show ads over legitimate app UI)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a modified app is launched, the injected code checks for infection, displays fraudulent advertisements as overlays to the user, and sends ad impression and click data to attacker-controlled servers, resulting in illicit ad revenue generation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code displays ads outside the legitimate app context and communicates with unknown servers, which is characteristic of adware and click fraud operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps display ads only within their own context and report to authorized ad networks, not to attacker-controlled infrastructure or via injected code in unrelated apps.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate ad-supported apps display ads within their own UI and report to official ad networks, but do not inject ad code into other apps or report to unauthorized endpoints.
key_indicators: Fraudulent ad display via overlays in modified apps
Network communication with attacker-controlled ad servers
Ad impression/click reporting to non-legitimate ad networks
Injected code present in classes.dex of tampered APKs

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly innocent app from Google Play Store or 9Apps containing the Agent Smith malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware gains execution on the device.

attack_chain.action: Malware scans the device for pre-installed applications and injects malicious ad code into them, replacing the original APKs with tampered versions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Modified apps containing injected adware are now present on the device.

attack_chain.action: When the user launches a modified app, the injected code displays fraudulent ads as overlays and reports ad activity to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker generates illicit ad revenue and maintains persistence via multiple infected apps.

behavioral_signatures: App attempts to modify or replace other installed application APKs in /data/app/
Injected code in unrelated apps displays unexpected ads as overlays
Multiple unrelated apps initiate network traffic to the same suspicious ad reporting domains
file_indicators: APK files in /data/app/ with unexpected code sections or additional ad libraries
Modified app signatures that do not match official versions from Google Play or 9Apps
Presence of duplicate or tampered APKs in /data/app/ with altered classes.dex
Unusual permissions granted to non-system apps (e.g., install/uninstall packages)
network_indicators: Outbound connections from multiple apps to attacker-controlled ad servers or domains not associated with legitimate ad networks
Ad impression and click reporting endpoints that are not part of known ad network infrastructure
Consistent C2 communication patterns from modified apps to the same set of suspicious IPs or domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that attempt to modify or replace other installed applications, especially those injecting ad code into unrelated APKs. Analyze APKs in /data/app/ for unexpected code sections, additional ad libraries, or mismatched digital signatures. Detect network traffic from multiple unrelated apps to the same suspicious ad reporting domains or IPs not associated with legitimate ad networks. Flag apps with duplicate or tampered APKs, altered classes.dex files, or unusual permissions such as install/uninstall packages. Correlate behavioral, file, and network indicators to identify devices compromised by Agent Smith.
